question: If a stone is thrown up, the value of acceleration due to gravity ‘g’ will be taken as _______.
solution:
The Correct answer is __**Negative**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When a stone is thrown upward, the direction of motion is opposite to the direction of **gravitational force.**
 
• The acceleration due to gravity (**g**) always acts in the downward direction, i.e., towards the center of the Earth.
 
• In this scenario, since the upward motion of the stone is opposite to the direction of gravity, the value of **g** becomes **negative**.
 
• The negative sign indicates the opposing direction of the gravitational force relative to the motion of the object.
 
• As the stone rises, its velocity decreases due to the negative acceleration until it reaches the highest point, where the velocity becomes **zero.**
 
• Once the stone starts to fall back down, the acceleration due to gravity acts in the same direction as its motion, and the value of **g** becomes **positive.**
 
• This principle is based on the laws of motion and Newton’s universal law of gravitation.
 
• Understanding the sign convention of **g** is crucial for solving various problems in physics, such as projectile motion, free fall, and other kinematic calculations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• ** Infinite**__

 __
 
• The term **infinite** is not applicable in this context as the acceleration due to gravity (**g**) has a fixed value near the Earth's surface, approximately **9.8 m/s².**
 
• **Infinity** generally refers to an unbounded or limitless value, which does not describe gravitational acceleration.
 
 
 
• **Zero**__
 __
 
• The value of **g** cannot be **zero** as long as the object is within the influence of Earth's gravity.
 
• **Zero gravitational acceleration** would only occur in deep space, far away from any massive object exerting a gravitational pull.
 
 
 
• **Positive**__
 
 
• The value of **g** is considered **positive** when the motion of the object is in the same direction as the gravitational force.
 
• In this case, when the stone is falling back down, the acceleration due to gravity becomes **positive.**
